title: Stories
description: The backlog a team can take: one epic per functional requirement inside the MVP line, stories that are vertical slices a person would notice, scenarios in declarative Gherkin that each prove one criterion. Every criterion inside the line is proved by a scenario; every story pins the criteria it proves and the screens it happens on. The writer composes epics, stories, notes and open questions; the runner owns identity, traces and the hash.

traces.description: What these stories were written from. Either hash moving makes the stories stale, and stale stories hold every export (D05).

epics.description: One per functional requirement inside the line. Ids are sticky across rewrites.

title.description: What a person can do once the epic is done, in their words.

stories.description: Vertical slices: each one is something a person using the product would notice. Ids are sticky — the same story keeps its STORY-n across rewrites.

statement.description: As a <role>, I want <capability>, so that <outcome>. The role is a person; the outcome is why they care, not the capability restated.

req_refs.description: The requirements this story delivers, in whole or part.

screen_refs.description: The prototype screens this story happens on. Empty only when no screen shows its requirement.

gherkin.description: Given/When/Then lines, one behaviour, declarative: what a person does and observes, in words that would not change if the implementation did.

proves.description: The criteria this scenario proves, as REQ-n/AC-m joins.

notes.description: For the PM: where the prototype and the PRD disagree, which reading was taken, what was hard to slice.

open_questions.description: What writing the stories exposed that the PRD does not answer — as questions for the PM, never as decisions taken.

subject.description: The REQ, AC or STORY it concerns, if one.

blocking.description: True if the story cannot be taken until this is answered.

x-drift-checked.description: The pointers the content hash covers: the epics and the stories.
